approach: Coordinator requeue of the REJECTED r4 candidate (de02212a; verify-6 adversary breaks P1/P1/P2). (1) settle_offline_receipt() [forward-only 20260910120000, replaced in place on the never-applied file] now inspects the ticket's terminal ledger state on the not_chargeable branch too: a receipt naming a ticket the ledger already CONSUMED (another rating) or RELEASED (device returned it) is a durable conflicting_receipt HOLD with the ticket untouched, never result_recorded/reserved that contradicts the ledger; exact redelivery replays the hold. (2) POST /v1/offline/receipts: offlineReceiptReleaseLineage() distinguishes the reversible control-plane freeze (deny_new_authorizations=true, release approved, withdrawnAt null/future) from permanent withdrawal (withdrawnAt<=now). Chargeable work under a freeze is answered delivery:'pending' (reconciliation status 'pending', financialDisposition reserved / not_applicable for a Pro lease) with NO settle RPC and nothing durable, so the identical redelivery settles once the freeze lifts; abstentions still settle under a freeze; only withdrawnAt is the durable grant_revoked HOLD. Regressions: security_regression.sql U3 rcpt-11b (not_chargeable under a CONSUMED ticket -> conflicting_receipt, events unchanged allocated:2,consumed:2, replay idempotent; U3 durable count 22->23) and U8 (release t2 then not_chargeable receipt -> conflicting_receipt, no ticket movement, no shot, replay idempotent); offline_receipt_reconciliation.test.ts +2 route tests (ticketed freeze -> pending, lift -> replay+settle; Pro-lease freeze -> pending not_applicable, later withdrawal -> grant_revoked). residual_risks: A receipt during a reversible freeze is answered pending, the device keeps it queued and redelivers (same path as the unsynced-session pending); if the release is later withdrawn the redelivery becomes the durable grant_revoked HOLD. Mobile already treats delivery:pending as retry-later (W04-05), no mobile change.

The SQL function is the durable authority for terminal-ticket detection on every billing branch; the route-level freeze handling is defense in depth only (a caller bypassing the route still cannot record against a consumed/released ticket).
